one_month_reasoning: Nov 1, 2026 is a Sunday, so the window is marked at the Fri Oct 30 close. The fiscal Q1 FY27 report most likely comes on Wed Nov 4, outside the window. I checked the EDGAR submissions index myself: the 8-K Item 2.02 filings came exactly 32 days after the Saturday quarter-end on Nov 1 2023, Oct 30 2024, Oct 29 2025, Jan 28 2026 and Apr 29 2026. Q1 FY27 ends Oct 3 (a 14-week quarter in a 53-week year), and Oct 3 + 32 days = Nov 4. No date announcement 8-K or release yet (last year's came 14 days ahead). So I put ~10% on the print landing inside the window, down from 35% in round 1. In-window drivers are only read-throughs: supplier Q3 reports (e.g. TI), memory pricing and macro data. Arrow's Q3 also likely falls ~Nov 5, outside. I use 90% weight on a lognormal centred at ~$107.2 (+0.25% drift for post-guide momentum, sigma 0.102, close to 37%/3.5 = 0.106 trimmed for no event) and 10% on an earnings-in-window lognormal with sigma 0.14. The result is near-symmetric around today's $106.94 and a little tighter than my round-1 ladder.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28 adj EPS $11.35 x 9.5x = $108, 50%), mid-cycle normalized EPS ($6.90 x 13x = $90, 35%) and P/B (~$61 diluted-adjusted book by Oct 2027 x 1.6x = $98, 15%). That gives ~$100, about 6% below the $106.94 price. Per-share figures are now on ~86M diluted shares (cash-settled principal on the in-the-money convert adds ~3.2M net shares at $107), not 85M.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Forward (FY28, Jul-2027 to Jun-2028) adj EPS $11.35 on ~86M diluted shares x 9.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide $2.85 on 85M, then Q2-Q4 at ~$3.0/$3.05/$3.05 on ~86M. Management calls this the '3rd or 4th inning' with book-to-bill >1 in every region, but the CFO warned other price increases won't match memory's. This sits above the ~$10.5 FY27 consensus (thin, 3-4 analysts, lagging the guide) and near the ~$11.40 Q1-guide run-rate; I keep an above-consensus view because the guide alone annualizes above consensus.

inputs_detail.input: FY28 adj EPS (forward EPS a year from now)
inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 $11.85 trimmed ~4% for memory-price fade (memory drove about half of Q3 FY26 sequential growth, source 8) and double-order unwind risk (source 7), partly offset by data-centre mix. Consensus FY27 ~$10.5 (source 13) with only modest growth the year after supports not extrapolating.

The stock trades at ~10.1x FY27 consensus and ~9.4x the guide run-rate (source 13). The FY23 peak traded at ~6x adjusted EPS of $8.06 (source 14). Data-centre mix supports more than past peaks, so 9.5x.

82.07M basic (10-K cover) plus awards (Q4 diluted 84.69M; guide 85M) plus net convert shares: 9.25M x (1 - 70.27/107) = ~3.2M, since principal is cash-settled. Gives ~86M at $107, rising with the price.
FY26 sales were $27.6B. The Q4 FY26 run-rate is $33B and the Q1 guide implies ~$36B annualized; I take $30B as mid-cycle, between FY26 and the current inflated run-rate.
FY26 adj op margin was 3.1% and Q4 3.8%. Management's EC target is ~4%; Farnell made 5.9% in FY26. A mid-cycle 3.3% gives ~$990M adj op income.
FY26 interest and financing expense was $250.7M. The $550M 5.65% notes refinance revolver and securitization borrowings, so the total is roughly flat.
Midpoint of the 21-25% adj tax guide, on ~86M diluted shares including ~3.2M net convert shares. (990-240)x0.77/86 = $6.72, rounded to $6.90 to allow for buybacks under the $600M plan.

On trough or normalized earnings the market pays more than ~10x; the stock is at ~27x trailing GAAP EPS (source 9). I use 13x for normalized earnings, in line with analysts' pre-upcycle targets of ~$80 on ~$6-8 EPS (source 10).

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: P/B: equity $5.02B / 82.07M basic = $61.2, grown to ~$63 basic by Oct 2027, ~$61 on a diluted basis (convert premium shares carry no equity), x 1.6x

inputs_detail.derivation: Book grows ~$2/share net of dividends ($1.40/yr) and buybacks ($225.8M authorization left). Projected ROE is ~18% on $12 EPS, which supports 1.5-1.8x book; I use 1.6x to allow for ROE fading back toward the FY26 ~7% GAAP level. Applied to ~$61 diluted book (round 1 used $63 basic).

bear.story: Memory pricing reverses and safety-stock or double orders unwind in 2027. Sales growth turns negative by mid-2027, and the market prices FY28 EPS of ~$7.5-8 at ~9x (or ~6x the run-rate, the FY23-peak multiple). Working-capital build keeps net debt above the $3.06B reported at FY26 year-end.

base.story: FY27 adj EPS of ~$11.85 is delivered (above the ~$10.5 consensus), but by late 2027 investors look through to a plateau. The P/E compresses to ~9.3-9.5x on FY28 EPS of ~$11.35 over ~86M diluted shares, so the stock ends about flat, with the ~1.3% dividend on top.

bull.story: The upcycle runs longer. Lead-time stretch spreads to analog, IP&E and discretes, data-centre mix rises and EC margin goes above 4.5%. FY28 EPS reaches ~$13.8 at 10.5x.

thesis_break_reason: $71 is ~6.2x the ~$11.40 Q1-guide run-rate, close to the ~6x the market paid on FY23 peak adjusted EPS ($8.06), and ~6.3x my FY27 $11.85. At that level the market would be saying the cycle has peaked: book-to-bill below 1, a sequential guide-down, memory price reversal or a double-order unwind with inventory write-downs. That is beyond ordinary 37%-vol noise (a 1-sigma annual down move is ~$74). A Q2 or Q3 FY27 guide implying sequential decline, or EC margin back below 3%, would confirm it. I keep $71, not the supervisor's $70, because my FY27 EPS is a little higher. The difference is immaterial.

catalysts.event: Q1 FY27 results and Q2 guidance (14-week quarter ended Oct 3, 2026; guide $9.0-9.3B sales, $2.80-2.90 EPS). Probably just after the 1-month mark (~10% inside).

Q3 FY27 results; book-to-bill and lead-time trend

key_uncertainties: How much of the 48% growth is price (memory) versus volume, and how fast the price part reverses
Double-ordering or safety-stock build by customers: classic distributor cycle-peak risk (management acknowledged it)

Working capital: FY26 operating cash flow was -$280.9M and net debt $3.06B at Jun 27, 2026 (likely higher after Q1). The in-the-money 1.75% convert (conversion price $70.27, cash-settled principal) adds ~3.2M net shares at $107, more if the stock rises.
What multiple the market pays at peak earnings: history says low (6-9x), while AI/data-centre exposure (10-15%) argues higher
Exact Q1 FY27 report date: the 32-day cadence points to Nov 4, outside the 1-month window, but it is not yet announced
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my primary-source figures: Q4 FY26 sales $8,295.4M (+48%), adj EPS $2.28, Q1 guide $9.0-9.3B and $2.80-2.90 on 85M shares, debt $3,212.8M, cash $155.4M, OCF -$280.9M, convert at $70.27. It flagged three things, which I act on. (1) Earnings date: I re-checked the EDGAR submissions index. The 8-K 2.02 filings fell 32 days after quarter-end in each of the last five Q1-Q3 quarters, so the Q1 FY27 report should come ~Nov 4, after the Oct 30 mark. I cut the in-window probability from 35% to 10% and the 1-month sigma from 0.11 to ~0.102 (plus a 10% earnings-in-window component), which tightens both 1-month tails. (2) Diluted shares are ~86M, not 85M, because the convert's principal is cash-settled and only the ~3.2M net premium shares dilute. That lowers per-share EPS ~1.2% and each method by $1-3. Fair value goes from $101 to $100 (P/E $108, normalized $90, P/B $98). (3) My 12-month ladder was the most bullish of the five (P>=107 = 0.505) despite a fair value below the price. I agree this was inconsistent: my lognormal median of $106 and base case of $108 sat above my own fair value. I now centre the lognormal at $104 (sigma 0.36), between the $100 fair value and the price, and set scenarios at $70/$106/$146 at 25/50/25. Averaging the two gives a median of ~$104.5 and P(>=107) = 0.475. I also take the supervisor's ~$10.5 FY27 consensus (thin, 3-4 analysts) as context. My FY27 EPS of $11.85 stays above it because the Q1 guide alone annualizes to $11.40 and book-to-bill is >1 in all regions, so I disagree with any implication that consensus is the better anchor. I keep the 9.5x forward multiple: the stock is ~10x consensus today against ~6x at the FY23 peak ($8.06 adjusted EPS), and the data-centre mix argues for some premium to past peaks. Thesis break is $71 (~6.2x run-rate). Further research was limited to one EDGAR check; I did not re-find a full Q4 call transcript, so the memory-share figure still rests on the Q3 transcript.
